bullets.detail: It was one of those suspended moments – I sat still, my thumb scrolling across the screen. The strange thing is this: you know no one is online, no new messages, no new stories. And, still, you scroll, in hopes that something – anything – might confirm the world you left behind hasn’t simply vanished. I came across a cooking video my mother had liked before we lost the connection. Seeing her name beneath the post struck me, as if someone had brought news. My eyes filled. I read the recipe for pasta with white sauce in the caption. She must have saved it for one of those evenings when she didn’t know what to cook. I took a screenshot, as if I might need to return to it – something I didn’t want to lose: yadgari, a keepsake, a trace of her touch pressed into a screen.

After 10 years of living in India, my connection to home in Iran had settled into a rhythm. Each morning, I checked our family groups on the messaging app Telegram to see what had unfolded while I slept. During the day, a message from my mother, a brief pause in the flow of things, felt like a small gift.

picks.title: Two probes are about to arrive at Mercury for an up-close look at this puzzling planet
picks.headline: Two probes are about to arrive at Mercury for an up-close look at this puzzling planet

bullets.point: After eight years of a winding journey across the inner Solar System, a new spacecraft is about to arrive at Mercury—or rather, two spacecraft, one from Europe and one from…
bullets.detail: After eight years of a winding journey across the inner Solar System, a new spacecraft is about to arrive at Mercury—or rather, two spacecraft, one from Europe and one from Japan, that have traveled together for eight years over some six billion miles (10 billion kilometers). They will be our first visitors to Mercury in more than a decade as they pursue a mission to scour this strange world in greater detail than ever before. What they discover could help enable something unprecedented: a first-ever lander on Mercury. The mission, called BepiColombo, is due to enter into orbit around Mercury on November 21 after an almighty trek. The two spacecraft launched entwined from Earth in October 2018 and have since completed nine planetary flybys—one of Earth, two of Venus and six of Mercury—to gradually slow their precession enough to be captured by Mercury’s orbit.

bullets.detail: The mission, called BepiColombo, is due to enter into orbit around Mercury on November 21 after an almighty trek. The two spacecraft launched entwined from Earth in October 2018 and have since completed nine planetary flybys—one of Earth, two of Venus and six of Mercury—to gradually slow their precession enough to be captured by Mercury’s orbit. The last spacecraft to visit Mercury, and the only prior spacecraft to orbit it, was NASA’s MESSENGER mission, which circled the planet from 2011 to 2015. The only other spacecraft to venture there, one of the most difficult places to reach in the solar system, given its proximity to the sun, was NASA’s Mariner 10, which flew by Mercury three times in 1974 and 1975.
